name: Migrant-Worker Work-Permit Renewal Desk for Small Employers (Lao, Myanmar, Vietnamese; e-WorkPermit)
buyer: Small employers and household or farm employers with registered Lao, Myanmar or Vietnamese workers (construction subcontractors, farms, restaurants, workshops), plus small labour agents who file on their behalf
trigger: Cabinet resolution of 14 Jul 2026 and the DOE notice: permits expiring 11 Dec 2026 can be renewed one year to 11 Dec 2027. Filing and fee window 8 Sep to 11 Dec 2026 (cut-off 16:30 for filing, 20:00 for fee). Fee is 100 baht per application plus 900 baht per permit. Filed on eworkpermit.doe.go.th with passport, a medical certificate linked to DOE, health or social-security cover and a stamped power of attorney. Employer fine for unlicensed foreign workers up to 200,000 baht.
evidence: https://www.prd.go.th/th/content/category/detail/id/39/iid/531308 ; https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/news/news-update/1250827 (fetched; confirms window, fees, documents, system; does not state number of workers) ; https://www.thansettakij.com/general-news/657139
existing: DOE's e-WorkPermit (outsourced to a joint venture, Future Sky) and unnamed private agents. The search found no named employer-side SaaS. Reports of a DOE dispute over work acceptance in May 2026 and of a system outage (Infoquest) show the portal is not frictionless.
unchecked: Number of workers and employers due by 11 Dec 2026; whether the deadline repeats yearly (earlier rounds 31 Mar and 7-21 Apr 2026 suggest repeated cycles); Cambodian workers; named competitors (the one competitor search returned no employer-side software); whether agents already dominate; the one-off nature of the cycle.

first_check.duty: Employers must renew work permits for Lao, Myanmar and Vietnamese workers expiring 11 Dec 2026 on e-workpermit.doe.go.th. The renewal runs one year to 11 Dec 2027 under the cabinet resolution of 14 Jul 2026. Employing a worker without a valid permit carries a fine of 10,000-100,000 baht per worker, and repeat offenders can be barred from hiring foreign workers for 3 years. Renewal cycles recur through annual cabinet resolutions, and there are separate deadlines such as the MOU cohort to 13 Feb 2027. The fee and window details from the claim are reported by news articles. The PRD page returned HTTP 503, so I could not open it.
first_check.market: About 770,000 workers are due in this cohort (InfoQuest, Thai Post and PRD reports of the cabinet resolution). Ministry of Labour data from Feb 2024 put foreign workers in Thailand at about 3.29 million. The number of distinct employers in this cohort was not found; one report counts 81,551 employers registered on e-WorkPermit.
first_check.competitor: The free DOE e-WorkPermit portal is the official filing channel. Licensed import agents and registered "ผู้ดำเนินการแทน" (proxies) file for employers; one report counts 81,551 employers registered on the portal. Thai and English searches found no named employer-side SaaS for tracking expiries or renewals of migrant-worker permits. That is not_reached as a full vendor scan, since I did no regional vendor-specific checks.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. The 14 Jul 2026 cabinet resolution covers about 770,000 Lao, Myanmar and Vietnamese workers whose permits expire on 11 Dec 2026. Employers must renew through the DOE e-WorkPermit portal. Under the Foreign Workers Management decree the fine is 10,000-100,000 baht per worker, which corrects the claim's "up to 200,000". Cycles repeat each year by cabinet resolution, and several groups overlap: MOU workers run to 13 Feb 2027 and Cambodians follow a separate track. I found no employer-side software. However, the core filing job is done on the free state portal, and licensed import agents and proxies already file at scale. The buyers are scattered small employers who are sensitive to price. The opening is mostly a multi-cohort expiry tracker plus a filing desk, which is hard to tell apart from agents.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The main risks are incumbents rather than a product: licensed labour-import agents and proxy filers (ผู้ดำเนินการแทน) who already file for employers, plus the free DOE portal. I named no agent firm, so their market share is unverified.
challenge_check.reason: Nothing I found kills it. Thai and English searches found no employer-side SaaS for the migrant work-permit renewal cycle. The only tools near the job are the free DOE e-WorkPermit portal, which sends status updates but no expiry reminders, and generic Odoo passport-expiry modules (generic, so out of scope). Market: about 770,000 Lao, Myanmar and Vietnamese workers come under the 11 Dec 2026 deadline. The portal has real friction: outages, queue backlogs, and a contractor dispute over 715M baht in unpaid fees. Score stays at 4 because licensed import agents and proxy filers already handle much of the work cheaply. Each round is also a one-off cabinet resolution with shifting rules. Recurrence (Mar/Apr and Dec 2026 rounds) is likely but has no fixed schedule. Per-employer willingness to pay looks low.
